context: Animated world map that morphs between 5 projections (Natural Earth, Mercator, Orthographic, Equal Earth, Azimuthal Equal Area), coloring ~170 country paths by continent using a 6-category Tol muted palette, with auto-advance every 4s and play/pause controls
first_impression: Clean and focused — a single large map with a restrained palette cycles smoothly through projections with minimal interface clutter.
what_works: The 6-hue Tol muted palette separates continents clearly even at small country sizes, and keeping the entire visualization as one conceptual view (one map, one legend, one action bar) holds cognitive load well below any threshold. The morphing animation treats all country paths as a single gestalt transformation rather than independent moving elements, which preserves object constancy.
what_doesnt: Animation quality and smoothness cannot be assessed from a static screenshot — the per-frame recomputation of ~170 path strings could produce jank on lower-end hardware, which would break the gestalt effect and make the morph feel chaotic rather than coherent. Small European and island nations are nearly invisible at this resolution, though that is inherent to world-scale maps rather than a design failure.
